cards.explanation: The answer is unclean spirits. Jesus gives the Twelve authority over unclean spirits (Mark 6:7). That's real power, and it's His to hand out. Twelve regular guys walk out the door with it, friends, and I can't even get my mustache to hold a spatula straight.

The answer is False. Jesus tells the Twelve to take no bread, no bag and no money in their belts (Mark 6:8). So no money goes in those belts, friends. A belt with no money in it is just a belt, I guess!
The answer is staff. A staff is the one thing Jesus lets them take for the journey (Mark 6:8). Just one stick, and the rest of the gear stays home. That's what I call traveling light, friends.

The answer is just one. Jesus says to wear sandals, but not a second tunic (Mark 6:9). That means one tunic each, friends. What you're wearing is the whole wardrobe, and there's no outfit change at the next village.

The answer is stay. Jesus says, "When you enter a house, stay there until you leave that area." (Mark 6:10). So they stay put in the house where they're welcomed, friends. No hopping from door to door looking for a better offer!

The answer is shake the dust off their feet. Jesus says, "…shake the dust off your feet when you leave that place…" (Mark 6:11). Notice the dust comes off when they leave that place, friends. Dust, meet ground.
The answer is testimony. Jesus says to shake the dust off, "…as a testimony against them." (Mark 6:11). The shake isn't a gift or a prayer, friends. It's a testimony, and that's the word Jesus uses.

The answer is that they drive out demons and heal the sick. Mark 6:13 says they drove out many demons and healed many of the sick. Preaching wasn't all they did, friends. Those hands were busy all over the road.
The answer is oil. Mark 6:13 says they healed many of the sick, "…anointing them with oil." Oil is the detail the text gives, friends. The passage doesn't say more about why, so I'll leave it there.
